title: 研究报道的结构
goal: 区分研究方法、结果与解释；识别研究结论的适用限制。

points.label: 区分研究方法、结果与解释
识别研究结论的适用限制

sources.title: 大学英语六级（CET-6）：课表
sources.used: 研究报道的教学内容、知识点与练习规格

cards.title: 结构
rows: 确定研究要了解的关系
The team asked whether a reminder affected attendance.
The team compared two groups receiving different reminders.
说明测量或观察的结果
More members in the first group attended.
提出可能说明结果的原因
The researchers suggested that timing might matter.
The comparison involved members of one club.
cards.note: 观察结果和研究者的解释要分开记。解释用 might、may 时，选项也只能说可能。

cards.title: 常用表达
rows: The team investigated whether layout affected search time.
The researchers compared two arrangements of labels.
The results showed a difference in search time.
One possible explanation is that nearby labels were easier to see.
The study was limited to one collection of objects.
cards.note: possible explanation 只是一种可能的解释，还要有进一步的证据。

body.box: A team asked whether label position affected a search. Participants used either labels beside objects or a chart at the entrance. More participants in the first group finished within a minute. The researchers suggested that nearby labels might be easier to see. They did not measure where participants looked, and the study involved one room.

Which statement is an interpretation rather than an observed result?
1. Participants used two arrangements of labels.
2. More people in the first group finished within a minute.
3. Nearby labels might have been easier to see.
4. The study involved one room.

body.p: suggested that nearby labels might be easier to see 是研究者提出的解释，即第三项。完成时间是观察结果，研究没有测量视线。

cards.title: 常见错误
rows: Participants looked directly at nearby labels.
The result applies to every room.
Both groups used the entrance chart.
另一组使用物品旁的标签。
A pattern in attendance proves a reminder caused it.
观察到的关联还不是因果。

lines.text: A team compared visitors using a paper plan with visitors using a digital plan. Each group was asked to find the same room. The team recorded the time taken.

options: The team timed two groups using different plans.
The team recorded which plan visitors preferred.
The team gave both groups the same digital plan.
The team asked each group to find a different room.
items.why: compared visitors using a paper plan with visitors using a digital plan 和 recorded the time 描述方法，即第一项。

lines.text: In a fictional survey, residents who borrowed tools more often also visited the workshop more often. The survey did not establish whether borrowing caused the visits.

items.stem: What limit applies to the survey finding?
options: The survey measured neither borrowing nor workshop visits.
The observed association does not establish a cause.
The result shows that visits always preceded borrowing.
The finding proves that borrowing prevented visits.
items.why: did not establish whether borrowing caused the visits 表明关联尚未证明因果，即第二项。

lines.text: Researchers observed that more participants chose the shorter route. They suggested that the route might have appeared easier to follow, but they did not measure participants' impressions.

items.stem: Which statement is the researchers' explanation?
options: They measured how easy each participant found the route.
More participants chose the shorter route.
The shorter route may have seemed easier to follow.
The researchers counted the route choices made.
items.why: suggested that the route might have appeared easier to follow 是解释，即第三项。

lines.text: The study compared two displays in one small museum. Its findings describe that museum and do not establish what would happen in every larger gallery.

items.stem: What limits the generality of the finding?
options: The study compared only one display.
The study used only displays from large galleries.
The study established identical results in every gallery.
The study was conducted in a single small museum.
items.why: two displays in one small museum 限定了研究的场所，即第四项。

lines.text: A fictional survey examined whether people who used a neighborhood garden also reported frequent meetings with neighbors. The team surveyed members of one garden. More frequent users reported more frequent meetings. The researchers suggested that shared work might offer opportunities to meet, but they did not observe the meetings. The survey did not establish whether garden use caused them.

options: Frequent garden users reported more meetings with neighbors.
Shared work was observed to cause every reported meeting.
Garden users were observed meeting their neighbors.
Participants met less often when they used the garden more.
items.why: More frequent users reported more frequent meetings 是调查结果，即第一项。

items.stem: What conclusion is supported by the survey?
options: Garden membership caused every meeting among neighbors.
The survey recorded an association within one garden.
The study directly observed every participant's meeting.
All neighborhood gardens produce the same pattern.
items.why: members of one garden 和 did not establish whether garden use caused them 限定了结论，即第二项。

lines.text: Today I will report on a fictional study of the placement of information in a community swimming pool. The researchers asked whether the position of a safety notice was associated with visitors' ability to recall it. The question concerned the location of the notice, not whether visitors obeyed every instruction in it. To examine the question, the team prepared two versions of the same display. The wording and size of the notice remained unchanged. In the first arrangement, it appeared beside the entrance to the pool room. In the second, it appeared beside a desk where visitors collected towels. The team invited sixty adult visitors to take part. Half saw the entrance arrangement and half saw the desk arrangement. Each visitor saw only one of the two arrangements during the visit. Afterward, a researcher asked visitors to recall the main instruction on the notice. The team counted a response as correct if it included the instruction's central action. It did not count the number of words recalled. In this imagined study, twenty-two people in the entrance group recalled the action correctly, compared with sixteen in the desk group. The researchers suggested that the entrance might have been more visible to visitors as they entered. However, they had not recorded where visitors looked. The proposed explanation therefore remained an interpretation rather than a directly observed result. The study has several further limits. All participants were adults visiting the same pool. The team did not test whether the same difference would occur among children or at a different building. It also did not compare a notice with no notice, so it could not estimate the effect of having a notice at all. The groups used the same wording, which helped isolate the position being compared, but the study measured recall immediately after one visit. It did not establish whether the visitors remembered the instruction a week later. A later investigation could observe viewing behavior and repeat the comparison in several pools. For now, the finding is a difference between two groups under the conditions described. The team can report that difference while keeping its suggested explanation and the limits of the sample separate.

options: Two positions for one unchanged safety notice
Two instructions displayed at the same entrance
Two pools with different visitor age groups
Two measures of safety behavior after a week
items.why: The wording and size ... remained unchanged，比较的是入口旁和服务台旁的位置，即第一项。

items.stem: Which statement is a proposed explanation?
options: Thirty adults saw the notice beside the desk.
The entrance notice may have been more visible.
Twenty-two people in one group recalled the action.
Both groups saw the same wording on the notice.
items.why: The researchers suggested that the entrance might have been more visible 是提出的解释，即第二项。

items.stem: What limits the interpretation of the visibility explanation?
options: The team recorded where every visitor looked.
The notices used different wording in the two groups.
The team did not record visitors' viewing behavior.
The participants visited several different pools.
items.why: they had not recorded where visitors looked 表明视线解释缺少直接测量，即第三项。

lines.text: This report describes a fictional survey of travel to an evening class. The research question was whether the way participants traveled was related to how often they attended. The survey took place at one adult learning center over a single term. Its purpose was to describe a pattern in that group, rather than assign participants to travel by a particular method. At the end of the term, the team invited class members to complete a questionnaire. Participants reported whether they usually walked, cycled, used public transport, or traveled by car. They also reported how many class meetings they had attended. The researchers compared the attendance reports across the four travel categories. They did not ask participants to change their usual route or means of travel. In this imagined survey, participants who usually walked reported attending more meetings on average than those who usually traveled by car. The team also found that many walkers lived close to the center. The researchers suggested that distance might help explain the pattern. They did not, however, measure every reason for a missed class, and the survey cannot show that walking itself caused higher attendance. Work schedules, travel distance, and other circumstances could differ across the groups. The result is an association between reported travel method and reported attendance. It is not an experiment that changes travel method while keeping other conditions the same. The survey also depends on what participants remembered and chose to report. Attendance was not checked against the center's register. In addition, the sample came from one center during one term. A survey at another location or time could yield a different pattern. The team proposed a follow-up study that would compare reported attendance with records and gather more information about distance and work schedules. Such a study could help distinguish some explanations, although its own design would determine which conclusions it supports. The report separates the research question, the survey method, the reported pattern, and the possible explanation. It also identifies limits on the sample and on causal claims. These distinctions allow the observed association to be described without treating it as proof that changing a person's travel method will change attendance.

options: Only their distance from the learning center
Their assigned travel method and measured walking speed
Their usual travel method and meetings attended
Their reasons for missing each class meeting
items.why: reported whether they usually walked ... 以及 how many class meetings they had attended 描述调查方法，即第三项。

items.stem: What explanation did the researchers suggest?
options: Changing travel method necessarily causes better attendance.
The class register contained every reason for absence.
A different term would produce exactly the same pattern.
Distance might help account for the attendance pattern.
items.why: The researchers suggested that distance might help explain the pattern 对应第四项。

items.stem: What does the survey allow the researchers to conclude?
options: Reported travel and attendance were associated in this sample.
Walking itself caused every participant to attend more classes.
Travel method was assigned randomly across the four groups.
The same association holds at every adult learning center.
items.why: an association between reported travel method and reported attendance 限定了结果，即第一项。
